#4080. Nioh 3’s generous demo is out now, and your progress carries over to the full game

If you’re looking for a way to check out one of the biggest releases of early 2026, Team Ninja has made it easy for you.

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Another big reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

The demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

#4078. Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business Review - Delivering Where It Matters

Australia Did It: End-of-the-world Railway Defense Business is a game I catch myself playing in my head long after I shut it off. Though it uses turn-based strategy as its base, it expands beyond the genre’s regular confines, blending elements from roguelikes, puzzle games, bullet-heaven titles, and the tower-defense genre. The result is an experience that demands wide-scale experimentation and rewards improvisation.

In a post-apocalyptic world where the Atlantic Ocean has dried up, you risk your life to ensure your shipment reaches its destination. Riding from station to station by train, you must build your team amid your many missions as various mutated creatures, malicious machines, and coordinated soldiers attack your convoy. Lore is doled out piecemeal and serves mostly as background dressing, but each time I learned more about the world, I became more curious.

To survive the harshness of the wasteland, you must use cindermint, an in-game resource gained for surviving turns and killing enemies, to spawn defenders, with three base classes to choose from. The revolver-wielding Gunslinger is your primary damage dealer, while the Radshot applies corrosive radiation damage, and the Nomad offers a close-range shotgun blast with knockback.

Those base-level characters offer solid variety upon which to build. And that’s where the main hook for Australia Did It comes in: experimentation through combination. In the midst of battle, you can merge two units of the same level to create new, more powerful defenders, influenced by the traits of those used in the merge. At the onset, you can merge two Nomads to create a level 2 Nomad with increased damage and knockback, but the real fun comes in combining disparate units to create completely new characters. Even now, more than 15 hours into my gameplay, I’m still concocting new combinations I want to try on my next run.

By the end of my first successful run, I had multiple level 6 characters, including a railgun-toting heavy, mages who steal health from enemies and redistribute it to nearby allies, a drone that can move beyond the walls of the station to attack enemies directly, and, my personal favorite, a dual-shotgun-wielding one-man wrecking crew. However, many of these higher-level units also possess drawbacks to consider, like the railgun scorching all adjacent tiles or the drone running out of battery if it’s outside the walls for too long. Though I started keeping notes in my head about which combinations led to my favorite results, I was grateful for a comprehensive compendium that tracked the tens of unit types I unlocked through this rewarding experimentation.

The meat of the experience places your squad on a 25-tile square board with enemies spawning from the four principal directions. Thoughtfulness and positioning are crucial, as each unit on your squad possesses different traits and movement efficiency, as do the encroaching enemies. Basic enemies often make a beeline toward the station, while others may take a weaving route or keep their distance and blast you at range. Improvising and adjusting your strategy on the fly is the most engaging part of Australia Did It, and when you perfectly adapt in the moment, or escape the scenario by the skin of your teeth, there are few better feelings I’ve experienced in a game this year.

Your goal in this phase is to simply defend the station and gather resources to strengthen your squad before evacuating and moving on to the next area. Considering each unit's strengths, weaknesses, and capabilities while strategically positioning them around the station takes some getting used to, especially during the more chaotic stages. I fist-pumped as I watched the train pull out of a station that was about to crumble, and I lamented the loss of high-level units I had to leave behind to ensure the survival of the convoy. The process is ceaselessly thrilling, even as you begin to see how the gears work under the hood. I just wish I could say the same about the intervening train sections.

Once you escape the turn-based strategy portion, your surviving squad members hop aboard the train and chart their route. Using a basic map, you choose your next stop, with factors like enemy types and modifiers shown to you ahead of time. The top-down train segments between station-defense stages are largely passive; the units you evacuated from the previous station automatically attack swarming enemies with the same traits and perks they have in the main gameplay areas. You can aim a focus cone to instruct your units, but you’re at the mercy of the units you’ve brought. You can trigger an ultimate ability to send your defenders into overdrive, but I rarely needed it.

While I love the idea of intentionally crafting a team that’s good at both the turn-based strategy and bullet-heaven transport sections, I was never fully engaged getting from point A to point B. Instead, I often caught myself checking how much longer before my train arrived at the next station; these sections can be completed in a minute or two, but that doesn’t alleviate the feeling that it’s a step down from the other gameplay. These novel portions aren’t bad by any means; they’re merely an average part of an otherwise excellent experience.

Looking back on the hours I poured into Australia Did It, the forgettable train segments will occupy only a small part of my memories, just as they do in each run. Instead, what will stick with me for months to come are the creative combination mechanics, the outstanding turn-based defense system, and the thrill of uncovering the mysteries of this bleak, yet engaging world.

Developer DeNa has nailed the thrill of ripping into a booster pack through stellar animations. Everything from tracing your finger along the top to tear it open, to pulling a rare card, captures that childhood excitement we all still feel deep down when we get something fancy.

While the Cuphead comparisons are inevitable, which is why I've mentioned it straight away, Acecraft deserves its own props. Not only does it look absolutely fantastic, but it's incredibly fun too. It sees you taking to the rubber-hose animated skies to shoot down waves of enemies and tricky bosses in classic bullet hell shooter fashion. It gets fast and frantic at times, which only makes it more satisfying when you successfully clear stages without taking a hit, having expertly weaved your way through a hail of projectiles.

For those of you who don't know how it works, much like Mafia/Werewolf or many Space Station 13 modes, there are a bunch of human players placed in a situation who must work together to identify the imposter among them. Among Us is lauded due to its accessibility and ease of play, but for us, it's the mini-game tasks that really make it stand out from the competition - that and the silly execution animations.

If you're just starting, you'll try events that don't require that many cards, while older players will brag with their well-earned decks and unique cards that will brighten your day with their golden glow, even if you're losing. There are also PVE adventures every now and then, if you get tired of constant brawls with other players.

Despite the Ragnarok setting, it's all sunshine and butterflies here, and why wouldn't it be given all the adorable creatures around you? Collect Melomon pets, join a guild with your best buddies, or simply hang out around the campfire and rake in all those AFK rewards - the apocalypse has never been this cosy.

If you're a fan of card-based roguelikes, then you'll definitely want to check out Indies' Lies. It tasks players with battling through randomly generated encounters while building the most powerful deck they can along the way. Best of all, you won't feel limited by the presence of a paywall, despite the game being free-to-play with in-app purchases.

If you've ever had a passing interest in Pokémon's competitive scene, then you should absolutely check out Pokémon Champions. While it's not readily accessible for complete newbies, which is somewhat understandable given the multiplayer here is incredibly complex, it's far more approachable for anyone with passing knowledge of the main series entries. Plus, it looks great.

#4076. GTA 6 Drew More Than Half of Active PS5 and XBOX Players on Launch Day

A lot of people cleared their schedules for GTA 6, and apparently they meant it. New figures show that more than half of the active PlayStation 5 and XBOX players tracked by Circana played Rockstar's game on launch day. The average time spent with it was over eight hours on both platforms.

12.5 million American gamers plan to adjust their schedules for Rockstar's next big release.

As Eurogamer reported, Circana analyst Mat Piscatella shared the figures shortly after GTA 6 launched on November 19. The numbers come from Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, which measures what people are playing rather than how many copies a game has sold.

According to Piscatella's post on Bluesky, 61% of PS5 players active in the United States on November 19 played GTA 6. On XBOX, the figure was 56% of active players worldwide. That's a huge share of the audience for one game, particularly when people still had all their usual favorites to choose from.

There's an important distinction in those percentages. The PlayStation figure covers the US, while the XBOX figure is global, so they aren't directly comparable. They also refer to people who were active on their consoles that day, not everyone who owns a PS5 or XBOX. It would be wrong to say that more than half of all console owners bought GTA 6.

The time figures are just as wild. US PS5 players who launched GTA 6 averaged 513 minutes with the game running, or eight hours and 33 minutes. On XBOX, the average was 494 minutes, or eight hours and 14 minutes. That measures time with the game active, rather than proving everyone was at the controller for every minute.

Eight hours is a full working day, and that was the average time GTA 6 was running for the players Circana tracked. You'd expect plenty of long sessions for a release this big, but those averages are still difficult to get your head around.

Eight hours is a full working day, and that was the average time GTA 6 was running for the players Circana tracked.

For comparison, Fortnite was the next closest game on November 19, with an engagement rate of about 10% among active players across the tracked console audiences. Even a game that people routinely return to every day wasn't coming close to GTA 6 on Thursday.

Piscatella also looked at what GTA 6 players had been playing in the two weeks before launch. The top five were Fortnite, Call of Duty, GTA 5, Roblox, and NBA 2K27. It's quite a mix, and it says something about GTA's staying power that the previous game was still on that list 13 years after release.

Piscatella said he couldn't remember another day like it in Circana's tracker, although its daily history only goes back to May 2020. That doesn't establish an all-time record, but it's still a striking result for the period Circana can measure.

The attention around GTA 6 has been hard to miss even outside gaming circles. Lately, I've heard people who know next to nothing about video games bring it up in conversation. That's not something I can say about most new releases, even the ones everyone in the gaming community is excited about.

Rockstar also announced that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies before release and generated an estimated $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales, including preorders. As DualShockers previously reported, that made for a record-breaking start before a PC version was even available.

Sales figures alone don't show whether people actually sat down and played. Circana's data fills in that part. A huge share of active console players had GTA 6 running on November 19, and the PC version isn't even out yet.

It'll be interesting to see what happens to those figures once the initial excitement dies down. As far as November 19 goes, though, the numbers leave little doubt about where console players were spending their time.

#4074. Guide: 43 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's 'Adventure Awaits' eShop Sale (US)

Every game we scored 9/10 or higher, plus a personal pick

With Nintendo launching its Black Friday sale on the European eShop earlier this week, we knew it was only a matter of time before our friends in North America got some savings of their own. And what do you know, they have!

Nintendo's 'Adventure Awaits' sale is now live on the North American storefront, with discounts across a bunch of first- and third-party delights. It'll be sticking around until 2nd December at 11:59pm PT, so you still have a couple of weeks to make the most of it.

Just like with the EU sale, we have assembled the following list of every game in the Adventure Awaits offer that we awarded a 9/10 or higher. We've also added a personal pick from the 8/10s at the end, because we couldn't see it go unmentioned.

As ever, if you're looking to grab some eShop credit before diving in, we've got you covered with the following links from our store.

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim is a wonderful achievement for dynamic storytelling, as it puts forth a compelling and multifaceted narrative that’ll keep you guessing right up until the very end.

This excellent story, combined with enjoyable combat portions, a striking art style, and some top-notch voice acting make for an experience that you shouldn't miss. It’s the kind of game that’ll have you wishing that you could play it again for the first time, just so all its best elements could be new again.

Aegis Defenders is a fantastic game, brilliantly blending the tower defence and platforming genres in a unique way to produce a memorable and enjoyable experience.

Lovable characters, interesting lore, plenty of secrets, engaging gameplay, and gorgeous presentation combine to make this a must-have for your Switch, a real gem on the eShop.

AI: The Somnium Files – nirvanA Initiative is one of the most interesting visual novels we’ve played through in a while. The murder mystery at its heart is brought to life by some great writing and quirky characters alongside the satisfyingly integrated, beautifully balanced Psync puzzle elements.

Even with some minor control issues, there is a lot to love in this game, even if you never picked up the original. Highly recommended if you're even a little bit curious.

The Nintendo eShop would be a considerably more exciting and interesting place if it were packed full of games like Ape Out. It’s a refreshingly original experience that more than deserves a place in any Switch owner’s library.

Difficult, frenetic gameplay, strong art direction, and an even stronger jazz drum soundtrack make this the sort of memorable game that you’ll likely keep coming back to over and over for another few runs in arcade mode. Ape Out gets a strong recommendation to anyone looking for a distinct and unforgettable game for their Switch collection; it’s a bit of an acquired taste, but well worth your time.

BALL x PIT is a tremendous brew of so many ideas it ought to collapse under the confusion. However, it operates in such perfect balance that it appeals both to the one-more-go instinct and to more cerebral planning and creativity. Kenny Sun Studios set itself a heck of a challenge but, fortunately, hasn’t dropped the ball.

It's out on Switch 2, too - and the upgrade is free.

Card Shark is the kind of game that at first blush seems like it just won’t work. Lots of dialogue bookended by brief, simplistic minigame sequences seems like it would make for an experience that would lose its lustre quickly, yet we couldn’t put it down.

Witty writing, high-stakes gameplay, and a gorgeous art style all come together here to make for a game that’s well-executed and unique in its appeal. If you’re looking to try something awesome that notably bucks most modern gaming trends, Card Shark is absolutely something we’d recommend, well worth your time and money.

Catherine: Full Body is a fantastic revamp of a bona fide cult classic. With an excellent new character and several new endings slickly inserted into an already highly entertaining narrative – not to mention a slew of fun new modes – this is the definitive version of an outstanding game.

If you've never played Catherine before, then you're in for an absolute treat, and if you have, we'd say there's enough new content here to make it worth diving in all over again.

An extremely impressive first game from The Wild Gentlemen, Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best visual novel/adventure games we've played in a long, long time and one hell of an absorbing tale. It looks and runs great on the Switch, with only a couple of really minuscule interface issues which are easily ignored.

At roughly eight or nine hours, the story is surprisingly lengthy, but we were never bored and wanted to investigate every little thing just to wring out more precious droplets of banter and fascination. Chicken Police is a polished, captivating experience and we're very excited for whatever's coming next from this team.

It's difficult to get across exactly why Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is so good without spoiling vast swathes of it, so we'll keep it simple. You'll come into the game baffled as to what the writers were thinking with some of these characters, and walk away loving each and every one of them.

There isn't a single moment of slack throughout the whole 40-hour playtime, it has the most extensive post-game of any title in the series, and one of the best endings to any game ever made. Go in blind and we promise you'll be in for the ride of your life.

Dark Souls: Remastered is a faithful remaster of a touchstone in video game design that improves overall performance of the original release while preserving all of the character traits that made it such a memorable experience. While it’s no less forgiving — and its menus are a little fiddly — this slick Nintendo Switch iteration offers an excellent way to experience Lordran’s ultra-challenging odyssey in true handheld form.

Plus, there's a Solaire of Astora amiibo. Praise the Sun, indeed.

This is an excellent port of a game that feels like it’s found a natural home on Switch thanks to a plethora of control options and the console’s natural facility with vertical orientation. Short of popping your 4K TV on its side, Switch offers the very best way to play Downwell.

Its roguelike structure and twitch platforming might not be for everyone, but you should really give it a chance. For our money, Downwell is a modern classic that should be in everyone’s collection; for the pocket change asking price, it's a steal.

Along with the expected multiplayer modes (ranked and casual battles), Faeria delivers a compulsive, interesting and frankly enormously fun card battle experience. While not the easiest game to explain, it's an impressive teaching tool for itself, but never feels overwrought or tiresome in said education. Of the card games we've enjoyed on Switch, Faeria is easily the highlight of the bunch and deserves to do well. It's a full-featured package and stands out as an excellent card/board/strategy experience. If you want to play a fantasy card game on Switch, we'd recommend this one first.

Every now and then, a game comes along that captures our hearts and reminds us why we love the medium in the first place. Forager features wonderfully designed crafting mechanics, addictive progression systems and more charm than you can possibly handle. Although it has very minor drawbacks, there's enough good stuff present here for us to confidently recommend adding Forager to your collection.

Heretic + Hexen is yet another slam dunk for Nightdive Studios. This new release revamps both titles with modern controls, bonus content, and thoughtful changes to the core design that make each game a delight to play.

Granted, these are still FPS titles from the mid-'90s, so your mileage will definitely vary, but for returning fans and those with a particular fondness for old-school 'boomer shooters', you really can't go wrong. Now let's get a native Switch 2 port with 120fps please, Nightdive.

Invisible, Inc. is a brilliant little tactics game, right up there with Into the Breach and XCOM – if not even better. The bite-sized structure belies a deceptively complex and meaningful game, where all your decisions ultimately mean something significant for that final desperate attack.

If you enjoy stealth or tactics games – or you're simply looking for a way into either genre – then Invisible, Inc. deserves your attention.

In a cynical era where nostalgia is pumped for all its worth with endless soulless remasters, Katamari Damacy Reroll serves up an engaging and rewarding game that hasn’t let any of its original charm or personality be lost in the transition from one platform to another.

With support for gyro controls and multiplayer — not to mention a degree of performance that sees it run smoothly in both handheld and docked mode — this Switch edition is easily the best way to play it outside of blowing the dust off your old PS2.

Altogether now: Naa na-na na-naa na na na...

An absolute pleasure from start to finish, what Kaze and the Wild Masks lacks in originality it makes up for in the strength of its level design, responsive controls, kinetic move set and attractive visuals. Excellent, action-packed platforming through and through, with great gameplay variety and gimmicks that don’t compromise on what the game is best at — challenging, fast-paced obstacle courses and deviously hidden secret areas.

Easiest sell? Kaze and the Wild Masks is to Donkey Kong Country what Freedom Planet was to Sonic the Hedgehog. Don’t miss this one.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land is a great big colourful joyride of an adventure for our little pink pal.

This first fully three-dimensional mainline entry in the franchise is bursting at the seams with fun and inventiveness, managing to transpose everything we know and love about past Kirby games to this all-new arena whilst adding plenty of delightful new aspects as it goes.

Mouthful Mode is daftly entertaining, each and every level is packed full of secrets and dripping in wonderful detail, and there are enough side activities, collectibles, and co-op fun here to keep you entertained and coming back for more for a good long while.

Whether you're playing on Switch 1 or via the excellent Star-Crossed World expansion on Switch 2 (with upgraded visuals and 60fps performance to boot), this comes highly recommended if you're looking for a fun platformer to play with kids.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World (say that five times, etc.) gives you the base game at a delicious 60fps with a whole big bunch of new content thrown in for good measure.

If you've had your fill of Forgotten Land on Switch 1, there's nothing here to warrant replaying the entire game again, but the 12 remixed areas that make up the DLC are uniformly delightful, the new transformations are excellent, and there's even new challenges for hardcore Kirby fans to get stuck into.

One of the best games on Switch and one of our favourite 3D platformers in years, polished to a sparkly sheen and packing some meaningful new content? That's a very easy recommendation and a truly excellent addition to the Switch 2's early lineup.

Buy Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World

Mark of the Ninja: Remastered is an utterly stellar stealth game and it’s lost none of the magic that made the original such a critical darling. Strong art direction, an engaging story, well-paced open gameplay, and a slew of extra content all combine to make for a near-flawless experience that you certainly won’t want to miss out on.

We’d give this game a high recommendation to all Switch owners; it’s the best stealth game money can buy in the Switch library, and one of the best ones in any console library.

Metroid Dread was a triumphant return for both Samus Aran and developer MercurySteam. This is a hugely entertaining and exquisitely designed entry that was slicker than anything we've seen from the series so far.

With a bunch of fantastic new abilities, super tense and enjoyable stealth sections, plenty of great big boss fights, and a story that long-time fans will definitely enjoy, we can't really see how this one could have been improved. Pixel nostalgia and genre impact aside, there's a very strong argument that 2D Metroid has never been better.

Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom is a tremendous accomplishment. It’s a gorgeous-looking game with a fantastic soundtrack and does its spiritual predecessors proud by nailing the Wonder Boy mechanics while still offering something that will appeal to modern audiences. As long as you can appreciate that it’s still very much an old-school game at heart and you’re going to get some 8-bit era platforming trickiness as a result, you’re going to thoroughly enjoy playing through this adventure for the 12-15 hours it’ll take you to beat it. It may not be Wonder Boy by name, but it’s definitely wonderful by nature.

Jim came to Nintendo Life in 2022 and, despite his insistence that The Minish Cap is the best Zelda game and his unwavering love for the Star Wars prequels (yes, really), he has continued to write news and features on the site ever since.

Give us the Switch 2 Updates for Dread.....AAAAHHHH! xD

Not a bad price for Kirby and the Forgotten Land + Star Crossed World. If you haven't played it yet, this is a very good opportunity to grab a phenomenal game.

How does Slay the Spire only have a user score of 7.5?! What's wrong with you people?! I thought you were cool.

PSA regarding Faeria. I agree that it is outstanding game, and I’ve greatly enjoyed it - even as a solo player. But, last I checked, it still has an always-online requirement. Rather unusual for its genre.

Not a dealbreaker for me personally, but (understandably) a red line for others. Caveat emptor.

I picked up The Talos Principle and The Gardens Between on the cheap this week. The former will scratch my Portal-like itch for the time being.

#4072. You Can Visit The Original Vice City in GTA 6 With This Hidden Easter Egg

Patrick Souza is a writer for DualShockers who has been writing for over 5 years, specializing in JRPGs, roguelikes, and other genres such as MMOs. He previously worked for Prima Games, The Escapist, and The Gamer, and holds a degree in Journalism.

GTA 6 closely follows many of the franchise’s traditions, such as adding tons of easter eggs to be found. Many of them relate to past Rockstar titles, and a very dedicated player has figured out how to uncover one of the game's best-hidden easter eggs, rewarding you with some nostalgia.

Through his X account, content creator Memeio revealed that he managed to visit the 2002 version of Vice City and unlock Tommy Vercetti’s signature T-shirt and motorcycle in the game, while also encountering one of the game’s most prominent figures.

Sony is banning players for sending explicit images from GTA 6, despite heavily promoting the mature-rated game.

Players need to follow a very specific order of steps to visit the city in its original glory. Memeio claims that it took him 3 days of wandering around the map trying to piece out the clues and actually finding something. And looking at how cryptic figuring this out can be, I’m surprised it didn’t take him longer.

By first visiting the Radio Station in Key Lento, you can find a small room with posters, an old TV, and a power switch you can turn on or off. By interacting with the switch, you’ll immediately hear the Vice City sound effect for finding health, raising eyebrows at the spot.

The next clues are in the two posters on the wall. One is for LPL - Leonida & Light, the power company in the game, and another has a controller image, and it says “Lose track of time”. You can find 12 LPL substations around the world map, all with multiple switches or buttons just like the one in the Radio Station. The substations are also marked with letters on the wall, which spell “Life is passing me by”, a time-advancing cheat code in the original GTA Vice City.

It doesn't take much to figure out that the phrase and the poster are connected. The switches, however, all represent a different key on your controller. Almost as if you could input a command by using them. And you can do just that.

By hitting the correct buttons in each of the 12 substations, spelling out the phrase in order, you’ll receive a phone message from an unknown source, asking you to visit the Turtle Head Power Station between 7 p.m. and 6 a.m. If you do, you’ll see a strange portal forming inside the station, and you can jump on it for a true wave of nostalgia. You’ll be sent to Malibu Club from the original Vice City, with old graphics and all.

Hiding a game inside a game is just the thing that Rockstar loves to do. You even get to meet Kent once again, with his old VA and all. He seems to be doing fine, and he’s a lot less irritated than his last appearance in San Andreas. Which only makes sense, as this is presumably happening during Vice City’s events.

However, the visit is brief, and you’ll be back to the current timeline soon. But you’ll have unlocked both Tommy’s Hawaiian shirt and his motorbike for Jason when you’re back, so all that work wasn’t in vain.

You’ll see a strange portal forming inside the station, and you can jump on it for a true wave of nostalgia.

This is far from the only easter egg from the previous game you can find. The Hawk & Little Morgan revolvers’ description mentions the Vercetti State, which can also be visited in the game. This is the mansion Tommy took over during the game, and it serves as a hub throughout the story. Other iconic locations can also be found as you explore Vice City, albeit a bit different from their 2002 counterparts.

This was certainly one of the weirdest, most specific easter eggs I’ve seen, even for GTA standards. But it only shows how much Rockstar has dedicated itself to bringing a unique experience to their long-awaited title. Fortunately, it was much more than just a lot of money.

#4071. Bandai Namco Shuts Down Unknown 9: Awakening Developer Reflector Entertainment

Bandai Namco has announced it is shutting down Reflector Entertainment, the Montreal studio behind 2024’s Unknown 9: Awakening.

Reflector, founded in 2015, is a subsidiary of Bandai Namco that was acquired in 2020. Unknown 9: Awakening is the studio’s only released title, which was first revealed at Gamescom 2020 and released on October 17, 2024. The third-person action game is set within the broader Unknown 9 transmedia franchise, which includes a book trilogy, comics, and a web series, and stars Haroona, a woman able to traverse a separate dimension called the Fold. Haroona, played by The Witcher actress Anya Chalotra, uses this ability and other supernatural powers to battle a hostile secret society across India and other global locations.

Upon release, Unknown 9: Awakening didn’t make much of a critical splash; it currently has a 59 Metascore and "Mixed" Steam reviews. #4068. PlayStation Cancels In-Development Live-Service Shooter, Fairgames, At Jade Raymond's Former Haven Studio

PlayStation has reportedly canceled Fairgames, the long-in-development live-service shooter being made by Haven Studios, which Jade Raymond founded in 2021. Sony acquired Haven in 2022, and in 2025, Raymond left the studio, though it remained dedicated to developing Fairgames without her. It seems the story of Fairgames is now over, according to a new Bloomberg report.

The publication reports that PlayStation will not enforce any job cuts or layoffs as a result of Fairgames' cancellation, which comes as a surprise, and the studio will instead shift to support other first-party teams under the PlayStation umbrella. According to Bloomberg, this cancellation comes after a recent test of the game that allowed "thousands of players" to check it out did not deliver the results PlayStation wanted.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees today, according to Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

This doesn't necessarily come as a surprise. PlayStation announced Fairgames back in 2023 and hasn't shown much since, leaving many to assume development has been struggling behind the scenes. Since then, PlayStation has pulled back heavily on its live-service plans, which originally included launching more than 10 live-service games by March of this year. Naughty Dog's Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled, Bungie ended active development on Destiny 2, and live-service Horizon spin-off Hunters Gathering is reportedly being overhauled following poor playtest feedback, amongst other stories. Reading between the lines, many fans were waiting for news like today's cancellation of Fairgames to drop.

Still, in an era where games are canceled and entire teams are laid off (sometimes even after releasing a successful game), it's nice to see Haven employees are not facing layoffs.

#4067. GTA 6 Patch Plugs Several Severe Progression Bugs

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

You know what’s nice about Grand Theft Auto 6 having such a monumental, far-reaching release? No, it’s not the literal billions of dollars it’s bringing in, though I’m sure nobody at Rockstar or Take-Two minds that. The best thing about having so many eyes on your game at once is that, if any bugs were missed during the game’s QA testing phases, they will eventually be caught with an almost mathematical certainty.

Considering the sheer scope and density of GTA 6’s world, it shouldn’t be especially surprising that there’s a decent amount of bugs, errors, and assorted unintentional annoyances floating around, some of which are more severe than others, causing problems with the game’s progression and critical systems or even hard crashes. Thankfully, Rockstar devs are still in the trenches even after release, hunting down bugs as they rear their ugly heads. Feel free to make your own Starship Troopers reference.

In an announcement posted to the official Rockstar Support blog today, the dev announced the latest launch updates and fixes applied to GTA 6 as of this morning that squash several severe bugs. This update applies to both the PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series X/S versions of the game, and should either already be applied or ready to be applied next time you boot up.

Sony is banning players for sending explicit images from GTA 6, despite heavily promoting the mature-rated game.

According to the Rockstar Support blog, this new update covers seven critical bullet points’ worth of updates. First and foremost, an unspecified number of issues that, when triggered, caused the game to crash, have been dealt with, so it should be more stable going forward.

Next, a bug that caused in-game weather to stay static for noticeably long stretches has been fixed, so you should be back to seeing regular, consistent weather patterns throughout Vice City. On a more important note, another bug that prevented the game from autosaving properly has been patched, so progression loss should be less of a concern.

The most important fix in the patch squashes a bug that was preventing mission-critical phone calls from triggering. Players afflicted with this bug weren’t having phone calls that progressed the story or unlocked mission content come in, which was a major progression bug. On a similarly critical level, a bug that prevented players from properly losing their current Wanted level has been dealt with as well.

The most important fix in the patch squashes a bug that was preventing mission-critical phone calls from triggering.

Finally, in a couple of relatively smaller fixes, a bug that prevented players from using the deadlift bar in the gym, alongside a bug that prevented partners from handing over fence-able bags, have both been dealt with, so you can get your gains and sell your illicit substances.

It’s good to see Rockstar on the case, dealing with these severe bugs, but as I said, GTA 6’s world is gargantuan, and there’s probably going to be a lot more bug reports flowing in for the foreseeable future, especially if and when the game receives any substantial additional content.

In addition to the bugs that have already been squashed, numerous reports have been coming in around the web of other annoyances, confusions, and assorted weirdness. For example, some players have reported NPCs walking into walls, while others report small, incidental objects floating in the air.

There’s also been some reports of graphical hiccups, mostly related to unpleasant pop-in. Clothing and cosmetic items may occasionally pop-in during gameplay, large vehicles like ships and planes may pop-in at a distance, and character models may appear distorted or low-poly for a split-second when loading in cutscenes. Most of this stuff is incidental at best, with some like the unintentional first-person view bug actually being popular, but hopefully, if anything more severe crops up, Rockstar will hop on quickly.

Team Up to Survive the Swarm: Battle relentless Tem swarms solo or with up to 3 friends in intense co-op! Strategize, share resources, and unleash overpowered synergies to defeat bosses. #4062. GTA 6 Hacker Walks Free Despite Seven-Year Sentence, Just Days After Launch

The hacker behind GTA 6's massive 2022 leak was sentenced to seven years in prison on November 23. But instead of returning to prison, Arion Kurtaj walked out of Woolwich Crown Court that day, just four days after Rockstar's long-awaited game launched.

The person who leaked more than 90 Grand Theft Auto 6 production videos seems to be trying to reach an agreement with Rockstar Games

As Dexerto reports, the 21-year-old was released on licence after the court took account of the time he'd already spent in custody. He's also subject to a five-year order limiting what he can do online. So while the sentence sounds surprising, his release doesn't mean the charges were dropped.

Kurtaj was part of the Lapsus$ hacking group and had been detained for years while his case worked its way through the courts. In December 2023, he was placed in a secure hospital after being deemed unfit to stand trial. A later assessment found him fit to plead, and he was moved to prison in January 2026.

On November 16, he pleaded guilty to a series of offences connected to cyberattacks on Rockstar Games and other companies. DualShockers covered his guilty plea at the time, noting how close it was to GTA 6's November 19 release. His sentencing followed exactly one week later.

Kurtaj had already spent enough time in custody to be released on licence rather than sent back to prison. Walking out of court doesn't mean he can go straight back to his old online life.

He's now subject to a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order restricting his online activity, including a ban on using Discord and Telegram. It's a significant condition for someone who committed cyberattacks while already on bail.

Walking out of court doesn't mean he can go straight back to his old online life.

Justice Turner also warned Kurtaj about wasting his abilities on further offences. The judge described him as talented and urged him not to spend his life repeatedly returning to prison.

The case also involved attacks on Uber, Revolut, and BT/EE. According to the UK Crown Prosecution Service, Kurtaj's activities exposed sensitive information and disrupted business systems. In the BT/EE case, prosecutors linked his intrusion to unauthorized SIM swaps, which could let criminals take over other people's calls and messages. He also admitted to possessing a mobile phone in prison, an offence dating to March 2026.

Back in September 2022, Kurtaj obtained 90 GTA 6 gameplay videos from Rockstar's systems and posted the footage online under the name TeaPotUberHacker. It gave everyone an early, unfinished look at the next Grand Theft Auto, long before Rockstar was ready to show it off. Rockstar sources reportedly confirmed the footage was genuine shortly afterwards.

One of the stranger details is how he did it. Kurtaj was already on bail for other cybercrimes and had been moved to a hotel for his own protection. From there, he used a phone, the hotel's television Wi-Fi, and an Amazon Fire Stick to carry out further attacks, including the one on Rockstar.

The leaked footage showed parts of Vice City and early gameplay involving the game's two leads. Kurtaj also tried to blackmail Rockstar by threatening to release the game's source code unless the company contacted him. The 90 videos were released; the source code was what he threatened to put out next.

The damage wasn't just about fans seeing the game early. Rockstar reportedly spent around $5 million and thousands of staff hours dealing with the breach, according to Dexerto. That was on top of the disruption to other companies targeted in the same hacking spree.

Those clips spread across the internet more than four years before GTA 6's November 19 release. Now that the game is finally out, Kurtaj's case has reached sentencing too. He's left prison, but the online restrictions attached to his release will continue for another five years.

#4061. Best Netflix games available right now - From Into the Breach to Red Dead Redemption

Netflix isn't just a place to watch movies and TV episodes - it's also a great place for gamers to discover new forms of entertainment, with a large library of games from many different developers and genres.

There are numerous hours of fun to be had on Netflix for gamers, from action to puzzle games. On the next pages, you can find a list we compiled after carefully considering all the available games and narrowing them down to give you the top 10 best Netflix games at the moment. How to find and install Netflix Games If you don't have it already, go ahead and download the Netflix app on your device. Keep in mind that you need to have an active Netflix subscription for this.

Now, let's get on with the list of best Netflix games at the moment.

If you don't know anything about the Football Manager franchise, you must be either living under a rock or you just don't like football. But if you do like football and simulation games, then this is a no-brainer.

Become a club manager and take everything under your control, from tactics and transfers to team talks, scouting, and pretty much anything else that you can imagine.

You can start your career at any club in the world, as it supports every league and has real players. As I said, this game is a must if you are looking for a football simulation experience.

Download now! Football Manager 26 Mobile

You already know about Bloons TD 6 from our previous articles, such as Bloons TD 6 tier list and best towers to carry your rounds. In this Netflix game, you benefit from hundreds of configurations and upgrades, so feel free to read all the guides we've created to help you on that journey.

Aside from that, what you need to know about this game is that it's wild. You have a tower defence type of game where things get increasingly more difficult. Towards the last levels, some players even reported crashes because of how crazy the battles turned out.

It's one of the most fun and entertaining tower defence games out there, and easily one of the best games Netflix has to offer.

Oxenfree is a story-driven adventure game with elements of mystery and suspense, sprinkled with paranormal elements.

The story follows a group of teenagers as they face the repercussions of opening a ghostly portal on an abandoned island, while out partying one night. It's also got a smart chat system that lets players have a major impact on the tale's action and conclusion.

New graphics, a remixed soundtrack, a new epilogue, mysteries, and branching story paths can all be found in Oxenfree: Netflix Edition, which was published on September 24th, 2022. If you are interested in this title, here's a link to our full review of Oxenfree, where we get into specifics.

Before Your Eyes is a game with a major focus on storytelling and beauty. The actual story is a little dark at its core, but the way it is presented is far from it.

It gives players the opportunity to immerse themselves in an individual's life, as they journey across the River Styx and into the afterlife. That is as dark as it appears, but it has its beauty.

Before Your Eyes has innovative gameplay with real-time tracking of the player's eye movements and blinking to make choices that impact the outcome of the story. It's not something we typically see in your run-of-the-mill mobile game.

Krispee Street is an adorably designed hidden object game that is exclusively accessible to Netflix members. This title draws inspiration from a well-known webcomic, and its graphics don't shy away from showing that. It's really well done.

As a player, you'll have to figure out puzzles and discover well-hidden objects, and while it might sound like a piece of cake at first, it really isn't. Oh, and it also has a certain narrative that it manages to tell between the puzzles and hidden object games. It's really good, and a nice break from the classical, realistic hidden object game we're used to.

As a kid, you've probably dreamed of defending the Earth from various calamities or invasions and being a hero in the end. Well, Into the Breach will make your childhood dream finally come true. You're the last line of defence against the overgrown bug-like aliens that can crush a building without much effort. However, humanity has advanced, and we have huge mechs and other weapons of destruction because we humans are great at finding the best way to kill each other.

Fighting is done on an 8x8 grid that's similar to chess, with turn-based combat. As terrain can shift and create huge holes in the ground, it can be tricky to avoid them while facing aliens. Therefore, careful planning is essential to win every round, no matter what the end goal is. That's the only way to turn terrain shifts to your advantage, as gravity works on your adversaries as well.

Storyteller is a hit game unlike any other. It starts off pretty slow, with just a couple of prompts, but soon enough you will find yourself in a story unlike any other. The game is available on Steam as well, which is where it was first popularised.

The best part about Storyteller is not the fact that it's sort of a build-your-own-story kind of game, but rather its unique take on it. You will be in charge of making a plot for each prompt you're given, and sometimes these plots have a twist. Literally. It's one of the best Netflix games ever released, and you shouldn't skip it.

Red Dead Redemption likely needs no introduction, though we should take a moment to appreciate how far mobile has come before we get to that. The fact that we can now carry an incredibly complex and detailed open-world shooter like this in our pockets shows the leaps in technology since the game first released way back in 2010.

If you're somehow unfamiliar, it takes place in the Wild West and follows John Marston as he hunts down the surviving members of his old gang. Why? The federal government has taken his family and won't give them back until the job is done. Yeah, it's pretty heavy stuff and is a wonderfully told story. In some ways, I'd argue, it's better than its successor, Red Dead 2. I appreciate that’s a contentious statement, of course.

But it's not all gloomy stuff. Thanks to the open-world nature of it all, there's plenty of twisted fun to be had with tying people to train tracks and waiting for the next locomotive to roll through. Or if you don’t want to act like a Looney Tunes villain, you can swagger into a saloon, find a comfortable corner, and play poker for hours instead. It’s good fun either way.

Download now! Red Dead Redemption NETFLIX

Death might not be the happiest topic in the world, but that doesn't mean it can't provide some level of catharsis when handled well. Spiritfarer takes this complex life event and somehow manages to turn it into a cosy management RPG.

You play as a ferrymaster tasked with guiding the recently passed to the afterlife. It's not a simple case of starting the engines and sailing across to the other side, though. The spirits you encounter are somewhat restless, and you'll need to care for them as they make their final voyage. That means getting to know them and their needs, which makes for an incredibly emotional final goodbye. Still, it's that bittersweet variety of sadness where you'll be pleased you took the plunge.

Aside from chatting to Spiritfarer's lovable cast, you'll also busy yourself with fishing, crafting, mining, farming, and all manner of other things. Just because your destination is a fairly morbid one, it doesn't mean that everyday tasks can fall by the wayside, you see. They're still important and in many ways key to the relaxing vibe Spiritfarer offers.

I've had fairly mixed opinions about Black Mirror ever since it jumped to Netflix. Though there have been plenty of good episodes since that move (Hi, San Junipero), I mostly find the quality has dipped (What was that awful werewolf episode all about?). However, Season 6's Plaything does stand out as one of the better offerings from the later series.

Now, that could simply be because my opinion is swayed by the video game stuff or the fantastic performance from Peter Capaldi (The best Doctor Who since the show's revival. Sorry, David). But either way, the fictional video game featured in it isn't actually fictional. Sort of. That's right, you can actually play Thronglets! It's just these little critters don't plan to kill us all... I think.

Inspired by Black Mirror mastermind Charlie Brooker's obsession with keeping a Tamagotchi alive in his youth, Thronglets is a virtual pet sim that tasks you with helping the Throng thrive. They'll hatch from eggs before relying on you for food and entertainment. Do all those things, and you'll have an adorable little army (?). Just don't set them all on fire, alright? They don't take too kindly to that.

#4060. Starsand Island is a life and farming sim that isn't gacha, and it's out next week

Starsand Island officially has an Early Access release date, and it sounds like it won't stay there for years.

Though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access

Starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab says you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

#4059. Zelda Playable & Electric Ocarinas Will Initially Be Sold On An Invite-Only Basis (Europe)

And you'll need to pass the criteria to register interest

We've been keeping an eye out for news of Nintendo's playable and electric ocarinas going on sale in Europe for a good while now. It looks like sales are just around the corner, but you're going to need to jump through some hoops if you want to get your hands on one.

Both the Nintendo playable model and HORI electric version will initially be sold on an invite-only basis in Europe. You can register your interest in getting either model now on the Nintendo website, but there are some criteria that you'll have to pass first.

Firstly, you'll need to have a Nintendo account registered in Europe (excluding Norway, Russia and South Africa), have allowed Nintendo to process your usage information to customise services, offers and recommendations in your Nintendo Account settings, and have allowed Nintendo to send email recommendations about games, events, special offers and more. You'll need to have done all of that by 22nd November.

You can only register your interest if you have "reached at least 10 hours of play time in the Nintendo Switch 2 game The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time by 18/11/2026" using the same Nintendo account you use to register.

And that's just to get an invite. On the day that the products become available, those who are invited will receive an email with a link to purchase either ocarina (limited to one each per customer).

The playable ocarina will set you back £29.99, bundling the instrument with a wrist strap and sheet music for all of the in-game songs. HORI's electric option is a little more expensive at £41.99, but also comes with a dedicated stand.

Reminder Zelda: Ocarina Of Time - Playable Ocarina Available Now On The Nintendo Store

Have you registered your interest for either model? Let us know in the comments.

#4058. Marvel 1943: Rise Of Hydra Reportedly Still In Development Amid Rumors Of Its Cancellation

Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, new reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was quickly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

However, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance New Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no announced platforms.

Although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

#4057. Ahead of the Game - Sol Cesto is a creepy dungeon-diving roguelike with visuals you won't soon forget

It's all about descending into the darkness and discovering what lies in its depths in this week's Ahead of the Game series, where we tell you about a new mobile endeavour that's playable in one form or another despite its unofficial launch.

The idea of descending into the depths of the unknown is already terrifying as it is, but in Sol Cesto, you're doing so because the sun has mysteriously disappeared - and all manner of unholy creatures have taken over because of it.

I've always been a fan of roguelikes, so the genre alone already scores points in my book. But I suppose what makes Sol Cesto even more interesting are the visuals - in some ways, it reminds me of this Burton-esque puzzler, Jars, with its creepy-but-cute charm.

Now, there's absolutely nothing cute about the monsters in the dungeons here, but it's still pretty compelling to dive into the depths to take them on. The randomised elements come in grids and stages, where you can use rewards you earn to, as you might expect, strengthen your hero when you head back up to the surface after inevitably perishing.

You unlock more heroes as you go along too, with each one offering their own sets of skills depending on your play style.

The haunting music adds to the atmosphere, so if you're looking for horror-adjacent roguelike runs before rushing into December, this might just do the trick. So, how do you play Sol Cesto? It's currently got that "early access" tag on Google Play, but I'm curious as to what else Snapbreak is cooking up behind the scenes before this is officially launched. It's all pretty hush-hush at the moment, though, so if you want to get your hands on Sol Cesto before it's actually announced, now's your chance!

#4056. 8 Best Connections to GTA 5 in GTA 6

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Rockstar spent a long time working on Grand Theft Auto 6, and it shows through the games many small details. There are tons of hidden easter eggs and secrets scattered across Leonida, and some of them connect to previous GTA titles.

More specifically, there are a decent number that connect back to GTA 5. Have you ever wondered what happened to Michael’s boat? Who took the blame for the murder of Floyd and Debora?

Thanks to GTA 6, we now the answers to these questions, and there are many more connections to GTA 5 that you might not have discovered. Everything is connected after all.

If you played GTA 5, odds are you spent a great deal of time exploring the map and going from town to town. It was quite a big map, but you wouldn’t have spent your entire time in the city, so you probably recognize Grapeseed and the Grand Senora Desert.

Grapeseed is a small town in the northern part of the GTA 5 map, with it residing in Blaine County. The Grand Senora Desert is a much larger area, but it also resides in Blaine County.

While exploring the many buildings that you can enter in GTA 6, you can wander into a few trailers, and some of them have postcards that link Leonida to Los Santos. You can find postcards specifically for Grapeseed and Grand Senora Desert.

You get a lot of phone calls in GTA 5. Many missions start with you getting a call, and then proceeding to head to some location. Because of this, if you have played the story, you will have heard Michael’s ringtone quite a bit.

Well, if you feel so inclined, and want to stay true to the spirit of GTA 5, you can have Michael’s ringtone in GTA 6. All you need to do is go into your phone’s settings, choose the ringtone option, and then select the one called Wind Chimes.

This ringtone is exactly the same as Michael’s from GTA 5, giving you that classic GTA feeling from 13 years ago when you played the campaign for GTA 5.

With the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, it is time to look back and remind ourselves why Grand Theft Auto 5 will be remember for years to come.

One of the best easter eggs in GTA 6 is that you can find Michael’s boat from GTA 5, and you don’t really need to go all that far. In fact, you have to stick rather close to home, because it is sitting right outside Jason’s house at the start of the game.

Michael ends up having his boat stolen in GTA 5, and you never learn what happens to it. Well, it somehow found its way to Leonida and ended up in Jason’s yard.

If you decide to climb up on the boat, you can see that a screen is still active on it. This screen shows the shores of Los Santos from GTA 5, seemingly proving that this is indeed the same boat that was stolen from Michael all those years ago.

Do you remember Fabien? He teaches Michael how to do yoga in GTA 5, and is known for having some rather… suggestive yoga poses. Throughout GTA 5, you can perform yoga as Michael either at his house or at the peak of Mount Gordo.

Fabien has been doing well since the events of GTA 5, and you can see what he has been up to thanks to his article in one of the game’s magazines. This is also an easter egg that you can find outside of Jason’s house.

Go out onto the porch, and open the magazine that is on the table near the workout equipment. Flip through the pages, and you will find that Fabien has been doing well. He has been on an “epic pilgrimage of enlightenment.”

It is a little ambiguous as to if the Mount Chiliad Mystery in GTA 5 was ever solved. While there is a means of seeing a UFO from it, it didn’t have a narrative conclusion, so it is debated on whether or not it was ever completed.

However, this mystery is mentioned in GTA 6, and it is on a vehicle. You can find an RV in Leonida that is covered in phrases like, “Don’t be fooled,” and “There’s no driving away.”

What connects this to Mount Chiliad is the eye symbol. It is the same eye symbol that is found at the top of the Mount Chiliad mural, making it seem like the mystery was never fully solved, or maybe that is just what Rockstar wants us to think.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a nominee for Game of the Year. It was selected at the last minute, but there are plenty of reasons it deserves the award.

There are some small nods to GTA 5 hidden throughout GTA 6, and one that is easy to overlook is a small book review for a novel sitting in Jason’s house. The book in question is titled Lethal By Design: A Liberty City Memoir, written by Tom Everett.

This book connects to the events of GTA 4 and Niko Bellic - a fan-favorite protagonist. With that being said, one of the reviews is actually from a resident of Los Santos.

The review reads, “Illuminating, revelatory, heartbreaking, and pulse-quickening - and that’s before you’ve even finished the editor’s forward.” This review came from Alison Taylor from the Los Santos Book Review.

There is an obscure reference to GTA 5 in GTA 6, and it connects back to some of the promotional material for GTA 5. One of the trailers for GTA 5 featured a man with a newspaper on his desk.

If you are paying attention, you can see that the newspaper’s headline reads, “Aliens ate my prize [blank]. Of course, I have to bleep out the final word due to vulgarity, but it connected to GTA 4, and it also played into the insane satirical nature of GTA 5.

This same newspaper has returned, and it is in GTA 6. In a shack in the Grassrivers, you can spot the same newspaper sitting on a table. It is amazing that Rockstar remembered to bring back this strange newspaper.

Floyd and Debora Hebert were an unhappy couple living in Vespucci Beach in GTA 5. Their house is used as a safehouse by Trevor and their cousin Wade. However, they don’t survive the events of GTA 5, as Trevor murders them in a brutal off-screen killing that leaves him covered in blood.

It is never known exactly what happened after that event, but you can learn the truth of what transpired after the events of GTA 5 by listening to the radio in GTA 6.

If you listen to the crime thriller podcast channel on the radio, you will hear them talk about Floyd and Debora. It turns out that Wade got blamed for their deaths.

Like many games, Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of easter eggs for you to discover. These are some of the best Leonida has to offer.

#4055. Nioh 3 launches, immediately becomes the most played Nioh ever on Steam

Just a few hours after launch, Nioh 3 is already the biggest release in series history on Steam.

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

This already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. #4052. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.
