#4019. Guide: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a dense adventure with many secrets to find, and while the critical path is fairly linear, it's rarely straightforward - asking you to pick up select items and upgrades before you can start exploring its many dungeons.

That's why a Zelda: Ocarina of Time walkthrough comes in handy. Though the Switch 2 version follows the same beats as the N64 original, we'd estimate around 10% of the game's puzzles and locations have been changed or updated - just enough to throw off those very familiar with the 1998 version.

This page features both an abridged and thorough walkthrough covering the critical path, plus a repository of our other Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides, from optional side-quests to items and collectables.

On this page: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

If you want brief directions and as few spoilers as possible in terms of item unlocks and progression, then use the following abridged walkthrough to take you through the game. If you want extra specifics - including useful optional extras as you go - then check the following section.

For a more detailed walkthrough of the critical path, this section can explain specific steps on how to progress. If you want even more detailed step-by-step guides to the game's many dungeons, then follow the links to dedicated pages on each.

Before you can visit the Great Deku Tree, you must find a Sword and Shield, otherwise Mido won’t let you through. You can find the Kokori Sword in the Forest Training Center to the southwest (crawl through the vent to get there, then find it in the chest above), and the Deku Shield from the shop in the northeast by collecting Rupees found scattered around the village.

Visit the Deku Tree, complete the Great Deku Tree dungeon, and get the Kokiri’s Emerald key item and an instruction to head to Hyrule Castle. Now leave Kokiri Forest to the west to receive an Ocarina in a cutscene before leaving to Hyrule Field.

Head directly north along the path until you reach the castle drawbridge. The area inside is the Hyrule Castle Market - there’s lots of optional activities here, including the chance to get your first Bottle from the Potion Shop - and when ready, proceed to Hyrule Castle, where after getting the Weird Egg from Maron, you must make your way through the grounds to meet Zelda.

You'll now have Zelda’s Letter and learnt Zelda’s Lullaby on the Ocarina. The critical path is to Death Mountain via Kakariko Village, though you should visit the Lost Woods first (for Saria's Song, which you'll need shortly) and ideally, an optional visit to Lon Lon Ranch (for a Bottle and the first step in how to get Epona).

When ready, go east from Hyrule Field’s drawbridge and up the steps to Kakariko Village.

After finding all Cucco locations for a Bottle and visiting the Graveyard for the Sun’s Song (both optional), show Zelda’s Letter to the guard at the north exit. He gives you an optional errand - returning to the Hyrule Castle Market for a "proper shield" (the Hylian Shield) and also to start the Happy Mask Shop quest.

Guide All Great Fairy Fountain Locations In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Powerful upgrades for a small fee? Fairy 'nough

The aim is to reach Goron City. Hug the rightmost wall: this will take you up and round the corner, then back on yourself up the cliff. The path will now split: take the left branch to Goron City.

Inside Goron City, head to the lowest level, where on the north side is a closed door. Play Zelda’s Lullaby here to open it. Inside is Darunia. Talk to him, then play Saria’s Song (which you can get from the Lost Woods). This will see you unlock the Goron’s Bracelet, allowing you to use Bomb Flowers.

Now leave Goron City the way you came (the top entrance), then go directly right to see a Bomb Flower near a fence. Now you have the Goron's Bracelet, throw it over and you’ll bomb the entrance to Dodongo Cavern, allowing you to enter.

Once you have completed the Dodongo Cavern dungeon and picked Bombs and the Goron’s Ruby (the Spiritual Stone of Fire), feel free to scale Death Mountain for a Great Fairy Fountain location (unlocking Din's Fire) before heading off to Zora Domain.

Zora River - which leads to Zora Domain - is just east of Kakariko Village and Death Mountain on Hyrule Field.

Reach the end - the way there is fairly linear - and access Zora Domain by playing Zelda's Lullaby at the waterfall.

Inside, you must find the whereabouts of Princess Ruto by getting the Silver Scale in a mini-game at the top of the waterfall, then by visiting Lake Hylia via the underwater shortcut for a Bottle with a letter inside. (Our dedicated Zora Domain walkthrough features more specific directions for all these, by the way!)

Speak to King Zora, Bottle up a fish found in Zora Domain, then give it to the giant fish in Zora Fountain to access Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly dungeon.

Once the dungeon is complete and the Spiritual Stone of Water is in your possession, head to Hyrule Castle. After the cutscene, dive in the moat and collect the Ocarina of Time, where you’ll then learn the Song of Time.

Head to the Temple of Time which branches off from Hyrule Castle Market. Inside, stand in front of the inscription at the far end, and play the Song of Time. Now go into the next room and retrieve the Master Sword.

After the cutscene, you’ll become Adult Link, and are told to head to Kakariko Village. Do so, then head to the Graveyard. On the left row of graves is a tombstone with flowers in front; push the stone and head down the hole. Now follow Dampe through the maze and at the end, you’ll receive the Hookshot.

To leave, play the Song of Time on the blocks, to emerge in the Windmill. Use this opportunity to get the Heart Piece opposite, then speak to the man to learn the Song of Storms - you’ll need this later.

With the Hookshot in hand, you can explore more of Hyrule, but when ready, head to Forest Temple: it can be found at the end of the Lost Woods, and inside the dungeon, you'll unlock the Bow and be rewarded with the Forest Medallion story item.

Complete the Forest Temple dungeon to unlock a Sage. At this point onward, upon returning to the Temple of Time, you can time travel back into Young Link by putting the Master Sword the pedestal. Also, to help, Sheik will teach you The Prelude of Light, which allows you to teleport back to the Temple of Time - a pretty handy shortcut.

As Adult Link, make your way to Death Mountain (it’s worth going into the Shooting Gallery in Kakariko Village now you have the Bow, which rewards you the Big Quiver to hold 40 Rupees as you go), then head into Goron City.

On the next level down is a Goron rolling around, and your aim is to detonate a Bomb near him so he stops. Once successful, the Goron will reveal their name is Link, son of Darunia, and will explain the Goron's plight.

Exhaust the dialogue options to receive the Goron Tunic - a red garb which allows you to withstand high temperatures - and directions to the Fire Temple, which is by heading to Darunia’s room (located on the bottom level at the back) and then by pulling the statue to reveal a route to the Death Mountain Crater.

Once in, go over the drawbridge using the Hookshot to meet Sheik, who will teach you Bolero of Fire. Now head through the left doorway, drop down and follow the passage to reach the dungeon, unlocking the Megaton Hammer and the Fire Medallion along the way.

Before you leave, it's worth going south across the bridge from the exit to Goron City in the Death Mountain Crater and using your Megaton Hammer on the cave entrance to get the Magic Meter upgrade from the Great Fairy Fountain within.

Head to the Ice Cavern, which is located in Zora Domain (or specifically, in Zora Fountain where you encountered Lord Jabu-Jabu as a child). Doing so will see you unlock the Iron Boots; make sure you grab a Blue Fire before leaving, and return to Zora Domain and use the Blue Fire on King Zora to free him and receive a Zora Tunic, which allows you to breathe underwater for an unlimited amount of time.

With both the Iron Boots and Zora Tunic in hand, we have everything we need to take on the Water Temple. Play the Serenade of Water to be teleported there when ready. Completing this will see you receive the Longshot - a Hookshot upgrade - and the Water Medallion.

Before we move onto the next temple, on this island is a plaque in front of you which hints at a puzzle involving the morning sun. If you are reading this as soon as the Water Temple has wrapped, the sun should still be rising: aim for the halo with your Bow and fire an Arrow, which will see it transform into a Fire Arrow on the platform ahead.

(As an aside, provided you have completed the previous three Adult Link temples, and have unlocked Epona, you now have everything you need to take on the optional Biggoron Sword trading sequence quest.)

Guide Biggoron Sword Trading Sequence Quest In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

When you’re ready, head to Kakariko Village as Adult Link. When you arrive, a cutscene plays showing the place on fire, Sheik appearing, and a spirit emerges from the well. You’re then taught the Nocturne of Shadow, allowing you to travel to the Shadow Temple - though there’s a place to visit you need to visit first - the Kakariko well.

As it's currently blocked off as an adult, you need to return as a child. If you haven’t already, learn Song of Storms from the Guru-Guru inside the windmill, then return to the windmill as Young Link and play Song of Storms back to him (now you have the Nocturne of Shadow, the return journey will be a lot quicker).

Doing so will cause the windmill to spin out of control and lower the water in the well. Drop down and complete the Bottom of the Well mini-dungeon to get the Lenses of Truth.

Guide How To Get The Lenses Of Truth In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

If you haven’t already, you also need Din’s Fire. This is acquired by visiting the Great Fairy Fountain location at the top of Death Mountain. Now you have Din’s Fire and the Lenses of Truth, play Nocturne of Shadow, then use Din’s Fire in the centre of the torches to gain access to the Shadow Temple, where you’ll get the Hover Boots along the way, and another Medallion.

With that done, it’s time to head to Gerudo Valley. It’s found in the west of Hyrule Field, and you need either the Longshot or Epona to make it over the bridge at the start.

Complete the Gerudo Fortress stealth section - essentially let yourself get captured, then find the four carpenters so you can explore freely - then past the Mirage Desert trials (you need the Longshot and the Lenses of Truth) to reach the Evil Desert Colossus area and the Spirit Temple.

This unlocks two new items - the Silver Gauntlets and the Mirror Shield - and another Medallion.

There are two optional extras in this region - a Great Fairy Fountain in Evil Desert Colossus (Nayru's Love; Bomb the cracked wall on the north side) and within Gerudo’s Fortress, the Gerudo Training Grounds (a mini-dungeon which grants the Ice Arrow).

Assuming you have now awakened every Sage and received every Medallion, it’s now time to head to the Temple of Time and start the final stretch of the game.

A cutscene will play and you’ll receive the Light Arrow, and an instruction to head to Ganon’s Castle.

Approach the lava moat around the castle to form a bridge with the help of the Sages. Now enter.

The Inside Ganondorf's Castle dungeon within is composed of six routes from a central hub, each with a 'Barrier' you must destroy; though you can tackle them in broadly any order, go for the Shadow Barrier first to get the Golden Gauntlets, which is required before tackling certain other routes in the dungeon.

Once that - and a brief trip to the Great Fairy Fountain just outside the castle beyond the bridge for a useful defensive upgrade - it’s time to scale the tower, or to halt your progress so you can mop up any remaining side-quests and collectables (see the end of this guide for a list) before the finale.

The tower within Ganondorf’s Castle is essentially a short gauntlet of battles until you reach Ganon himself at the top, and from there, it’s a linear stretch until the end credits. Good luck!

Here is a list of side quests, items and collectables you can find.

#4018. 2027 Video Game Grammy Nominations Include Avatar: Frontiers Of Pandora For The Third Time

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be announced tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

#4017. You're not crazy, trying to heal in Nioh 3 sometimes doesn't work - and Team Ninja is fixing it

One of the more insidiously aggravating bugs in Nioh 3 makes it so the game ignores you when you try to use elixirs, but hopefully not for long.

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

#4016. 10 Fun 2026 Games That Would Make for Great Holiday Gifts

Eric Warner is a Journalist and Multimedia Producer based in New England with over 7 years of experience producing stories for multiple publications

For many cultures and countries across the globe, the holiday season is in full swing, with many households preparing to attend family gatherings, celebrate events, and, of course, starting to purchase holiday gifts for children and other loved ones.

Several storefronts and digital retailers have already begun issuing early Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals, with many products, especially physical video games, going on sale for 25-50% off their original sale price.

With 2026 being a particularly great year for new video game releases, here are 10 fun new video games that were released this year that would make for great holiday gifts for loved ones of all kinds ranging from titles intended for children to those aimed at more mature gamers.

Mojang’s Minecraft is considered by gamers of all ages to be one of the greatest games of all time, and over the years it’s been expanded upon through numerous updates. If fans want to get an early look at the game’s first new dimension in 15 years, then they’ll have to check out Minecraft Dungeons II.

Like its 2020 predecessor, Minecraft Dungeons II is a third-person hack and slash dungeon crawler. It follows a hero as they set out to stop illagers from threatening the world with power from the new Warden-based Sift dimension, fighting a variety of new exclusive mobs along the way.

While Minecraft Dungeons II has only been out for less than two months so far and isn’t currently on sale, it would surely make a great holiday gift for any fan of Minecraft, especially kids, as it does feature local four-player co-op allowing siblings, parents, and friends to easily play together.

Avengers: Doomsday is expected to be the biggest movie release of the decade. While Marvel fans still have to wait till late December to see the film, they can quench their thirst for action-packed Marvel content by purchasing Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls.

Set in the Japanese anime-inspired Earth-358, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a 2D 4v4 tag team fighting game centered around the Fighting Avengers, the Unbreakable X-Men, the Amazing Guardians, the Samurai Outriders, and the Knights of Doom fighting each other to ultimately defeat the Champion of the Universe.

Marvel Tokon is easily the best Marvel video game released this year. Not only does it feature over 20 playable heroes and villains, but it also includes five distinct campaigns following each team attempting to defeat the Champion, with the best arguably following Doctor Doom and his cadre of iconic villains.

2026 has been great for horror titles, as fantastic games like The Sinking City 2 and Resident Evil Requiem debuted earlier this year. However, I would argue that the best horror game to gift horror fans this holiday season is Tarsier Studios’ Reanimal.

Similar in gameplay and visual design to the Little Nightmares series, Reanimal is a co-op platforming survival horror game following a young brother and sister as they travel to their home island to find three friends. Tragically, they find it in ruins and filled with gigantic humanoid and animalistic monsters.

Some horror stories are best experienced alone, but Reanimal is one that family and friends alike will certainly enjoy playing through together as they tackle puzzles and try to solve the mystery surrounding the island and its inhabitants.

This fall will be a lot of fun for couch and online co-op enthusiasts.

Millions of fans around the world love Star Wars. While Disney is releasing a ton of different SW products this holiday season to tantalize shoppers, people should consider gifting their Star Wars and video game fan loved ones with the surprise hit, Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

A roguelite racing game set shortly after the Battle of Jakku, Star Wars: Galactic Racer is centered around the rise of unsanctioned races via the new Galactic Racing League, with the protagonist Shade attempting to become the new Galactic League champion.

Galactic Racer’s colorful cast of characters and intense races utilizing podracers, land speeders, speeder bikes, or skim speeders have quickly made it become one of the most critically acclaimed SW titles in years. Fans will surely fall in love with the game for the hilarious character of Biddy Blas alone.

LEGO products have become a signature gift for decades now. While many parents will undoubtedly buy their kids a few LEGO sets this holiday season, they should also consider buying them the LEGO video game, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight.

Unlike past TT LEGO titles, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight isn’t based on any particular Batman movie but is rather a conglomeration of all things Batman, utilizing a gameplay structure similar to Batman: Arkham Knight while using elements from several Batman films, comics, and shows.

Legacy may not feature as many playable characters as past TT games, but it more than makes up for it by featuring dozens of alternate costumes for each character, alternate driveable variations of the Batmobile, and a customizable Batcave on top of returning two-player co-op.

Some gamers enjoy first-person shooters while others enjoy simulators, but some players want more open-world, narrative-driven experiences such as those commonly found in role-playing games. Arguably the best RPG of 2026 is Rebel Wolves’ debut title, The Blood of Dawnwalker.

Made by the creators of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, The Blood of Dawnwalker is a medieval fantasy RPG set in the 14th century kingdom of Vale Sangora, following a half-man half-vampire named Coen as he sets out to save his family and his country from the clutches of the Ancient Roman vampire Brencis.

The story, characters, and world-building of Dawnwalker are absolutely incredible, but it also has a ton of replay value as players can invest in witchcraft, sword skills, or vampire abilities and even accidentally drain the blood of NPCs if they don’t maintain their vampiric thirst.

As we approach the end of 2026, our lives are going to get even busier as the days pass, so why not add a hundred hour adventure or two to the mix?

Many older gamers are more action-oriented, and while 2026 has seen many great action games come out over the past few months, like Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, I would argue that best action game to gift gamers this holiday season is Gears of War: E-Day.

The sixth mainline entry in the third-person Gears of War series and prequel to the first Gears game, Gears of War: E-Day follows COG soldiers Marcus Fenix, Dominic Santiago, Mags Carter, and Lucas Reyes as they struggle to fight a horrifying invasion from the subterranean Locust Horde on Emergence Day.

E-Day may only be available on PC and Xbox Series X|S consoles, but it's by far the best Xbox exclusive released in years thanks to its gruesome, action-packed, yet emotional co-op campaign, thrilling PvP multiplayer, and addictive PvE Horde Siege mode.

With Legendary Pictures and Toho releasing several great Godzilla movies in recent years, many kids are growing up as huge Godzilla fans. A perfect gift to get them this holiday season is Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered.

A remaster of 2002’s Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is a four-player 3D fighting game with players being able to control some of Toho's most famous kaiju in city-destroying battles. Such behemoths as Godzilla, Rodan, King Ghidorah, Mechagodzilla, and more are playable.

What makes Godzilla: DAMMR an especially great gift this holiday season is its affordable price and small file size, with the game currently being sold on PS5 for $29.99 and featuring a file size of about 5 GB, making it a quick game to download and start playing.

Similar to LEGO, Pokemon has increasingly become a prevalent presence in households during the holiday season. While there are several Pokemon products to gift people this season, I would recommend people gift Pokemon Pokopia to fans.

Unlike the main turn-based RPG games, Pokemon Pokopia is social simulation game akin to Animal Crossing, with players embodying a human-imitating Ditto waking up in a post-apocalyptic version of the Kanto region and setting out to restore the area using its transformative powers.

What follows is an adorably charming experience as Ditto rebuilds habitats and befriends Pokemon from every generation, with people even able to create their own structures and minigames similar to Minecraft to play with friends.

From unforgettable adventures to clever dungeons, these games capture some of the magic that makes Zelda so special.

One of the best games to gift anyone this holiday season is undoubtedly the 2026 masterpiece that is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for the Nintendo Switch 2.

Released to celebrate The Legend of Zelda’s 40th anniversary, 2026’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a faithful modern remake of the classic Nintendo 64 action-adventure game, with the game once again following a young Link as he set out to save the kingdom of Hyrule from the evil Ganondorf.

Being a first-party Nintendo game that’s only a few weeks old, it’s unlikely that the Ocarina of Time remake will go on sale anytime soon, but it’s well worth purchasing at full price. Especially for parents who want to introduce their kids to Link’s most famous adventure for the first time.

The Game Of The Year nominees at The Game Awards 2026 have been revealed, and it's full of titles that launched near the end of the year.

#4015. Make Room For GTAVI By Deleting Your PS5 Trophy Clips

Hard drive space is a premium commodity, and its value has never been more apparent than in the approximately two and a half days leading up to the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is a whopping 209 GB, but thankfully you can purchase the game and preload it now – which you should do because who knows if the servers are going to be able to handle the strain of what is officially the most pre-ordered game ever on both PlayStation and Xbox platforms.

The easy (and likely necessary) answer is to delete the big games you aren't currently playing off your hard drive, but there is a cache of arguably unnecessary data on PlayStation 5 that might get you there before you have to make hard decisions.

You may have turned it off (Settings > Capture and Broadcasts > Captures > Trophies under the Auto-captures section > Save Trophy Videos under the Video Clips section > Change to None), which if that is the case, then I'm sorry. I can't help you. But the default setting which maybe you've never touched, is saving a lot of unnecessary video.

Every time you get a Trophy on PlayStation 5, it creates a short video clip that I bet you never have and never will watch. Here's how to delete all those videos fairly quickly to free up at least some space.

First up, go to the Media Gallery. The quickest way to do that is to press the screenshot button to the left of the touchpad, tap over to the most recent media capture on the left, press X, and then press the Go to Media Gallery button.

Next, go to the Trophies tab, go to the Sort and Filter option (the downward arrow with the three lines), and change Media Type to Video Clips.

After that, go back a few screens and go to the Select Multiple option (the overlapping squares with the check mark on it). Go ahead and press the Select All option, then press Delete, and then hold your breath and commit by pressing Delete again.

In taking screenshots to write this little article, I deleted 110 14-second clips. That's about 25 minutes of video footage, which ain't nothing. Maybe it will help you not delete that one game that you started three years ago that you are definitely going to get back to any day now.

#4014. 'Gears & GTA 6 May Have Provided A Temporary Reprieve' - Xbox Hardware Sales Get A Major Surge In The US

"Higher pricing was the primary driver of the dollar sales growth"

Xbox hardware sales were up 42% in October in the U.S. year-over-year. It's been donkeys since we've seen positive news attached to this level of stonks coming out of Microsoft, so we'll take it!

The figures were shared in a monthly report from the statistical boffins over at Circana. Mat Piscatella revealed that US hardware spending was up by 2% compared to October last year. PlayStation 5 sales grew by 20%, Switch 2 dropped 11%, and Xbox Series surged by 42%. Phwoar!

Hardware - Hardware spending increased by 2% versus a year ago, to $357M. October growth in PlayStation 5 (+20%) and Xbox Series (+42%) dollar sales when compared to a year ago offset a drop in Switch 2 (-11%).

However, Piscatella made sure to point out that "higher pricing was the primary driver of dollar sales growth" for Xbox Series, as "XBS unit sales grew by 10%" whilst the average selling price also bumped up by 29%.

Hardware - Higher pricing was the primary driver of the dollar sales growth on both PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series. PS5 unit sales increased by 5% versus a year ago, while its average selling price (ASP) increased by 13%. XBS unit sales grew by 10% vs YA, while its ASP jumped 29%.

Xbox's planned hardware price increase came into effect back in August, but according to Circana, Gears of War: E-Day and GTA 6 "may have provided at least a temporary reprieve" for the console's sales figures.

"It’s no secret that Xbox Series hardware sales have struggled in recent years. Gears and GTA may have provided at least a temporary reprieve."

Gears of War: E-Day appears to be something of a console mover, and I'd wager help from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 played a part too. Microsoft has claimed the top two spots in Circana's projected best-selling video games chart for October 2026, taking both physical and digital dollar sales into consideration.

October 2026 U.S. Projected Top 10 Best-Selling Games Ranked on Physical & Full Game Digital Dollar Sales (Excludes Mobile and Digital Add-On Content)

Modern Warfare 4 was the best-selling game of October, which Piscatella also noted makes it the "19th consecutive year that a Call of Duty franchise release has been the best-selling game of its debut month".

#4013. Sakurai Celebrates Kirby Air Riders' First Anniversary And Seemingly Ponders His Future As A Game Creator

He's apparently still working at "full throttle"

As we reflect on 25 years of Super Smash Bros. Melee, it seems game director Masahiro Sakurai is taking a moment to remind everyone that Kirby Air Riders has now been available for a year.

As highlighted by Sakurai on social media, the Switch 2 exclusive is officially one year old as of this week. It's received multiple updates since launch and Nintendo recently rolled out the last two amiibo.

In the game director's message, he also touches on his future as a game creator. Here's a rough translation of this part of Sakurai's post via EventHubs: "Time flies. I wonder how much more I'll be able to make".

Sakurai admittedly isn't getting any younger, and Kirby Air Riders included "everything" at launch, so it seems this is a genuine reflection on his future as a game creator. He has reportedly claimed to be semi-retired in the past, but this eventually led to Kirby Air Riders. He's also raised his future within the game industry on multiple other occasions.

Just earlier this week at the Famitsu 40th Anniversary Festival, Sakurai apparently revisited a column he had written about retirement, and how his decision depends on the demand for his work, and if he remains capable of delivering it (via OtakuKart). He's also questioned when his "spirit" might break. For now, though, he's still apparently working at "full throttle".

If we do hear any significant updates about Sakurai's future projects, or anything else he is up to, we'll be sure to let you know.

#4012. Genshin Impact Luna 5 takes the squad back to Mondstadt, finally makes Varka playable

Genshin Impact's next update will have you reminiscing about the good ol' days of... 2020.

The latest big content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

#4011. Star Wars: Galactic Racer Gets Local Splitscreen Multiplayer Next Year

Star Wars: Galactic Racer has been one of 2026’s breakout titles, but much of the game’s praise stems from its exceptional roguelike single-player mode. If you want to race against human players, you can only do so online. Thankfully, for fans of couch multiplayer, that’s going to change.

Developer Fuse Games announced yesterday that local splitscreen multiplayer is coming to Star Wars: Galactic Racer early next year. The mode lets you race up to three other players on the same screen. That's pretty much all there is to it, but given that local multiplayer was the game's biggest omission and, as a result, the most requested addition, there's probably no better news for Galactic Racer fans.

We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to develop a new mode: Free Play. Choose your vehicle, character, planet, and track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local splitscreen action.[image or embed]

#4010. Viral GTA 6 Competitor Gets Promising Anti-Cheat Update

Lauren has experience in the gaming and esports space, writing news, guides, features, reviews, lists, conducting interviews, and more. Before joining the team at DualShockers, Lauren was a Features Writer at Adventure Gamers, a Guides Writer at Gameranx, as well as contributing as a News Writer at PCInvasion and Daily

Rob Run is a free-to-play crime sandbox where you participate in bank robberies, raids, shootouts, and risk losing everything in lobbies of up to 5,000 players. Create your own hideout, upgrade your base, and even join a clan to become the most powerful crime family ever seen. It has a familiar progression system among fans of survival games, thanks to the presence of server wipes, allowing you to write fresh stories every time.

Not only that, but Rob Run has voice chat, so all players can communicate out in the world, set up RP scenarios, and share hilarious encounters.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

If you’re not playing GTA 6 or you’re waiting for the new era of GTA Online to begin, Rob Run is a solid alternative. However, the biggest criminals right now are the cheaters who are ruining games for everybody else.

At the time of writing, Rob Run’s Steam reviews sit at “Mixed,” with the vast majority of negative reviews pointing out the prevalence of cheaters. In response, Kefir has announced upcoming measures in an attempt to nip the problem in the bud.

The team behind Rob Run is prioritizing strengthening its defenses against cheaters, so much so that an upcoming update that’s expected to deploy new in-game mechanics has been temporarily delayed. As well as this, discussions are being had about increased security measures with the Easy Anti-Cheat team, developing their own cheat-detection tools, and expanding the in-house anti-cheat team to deal with the onslaught of hackers.

According to Kefir, they have banned over 200,000 accounts so far, but “we know that in a free-to-play game, a standard ban isn't enough — cheaters can quickly create a new account and jump right back in. To combat this, we’re exploring hardware bans. Because separate servers with stricter access requirements can be launched much faster, we plan to roll those out first.”

The first planned solution is to make server access require either a minimum amount of jail time or a certain total of in-game purchases. Unlike the majority of other crime games, jail time is actually something you want to grow in Rob Run. The more wealth you have when the wipe sweeps in, the longer your prison sentence will be.

Players on these restricted servers will be matchmade separately from standard servers, including in Looty Bay. Depending on the minimum amount of jail time required, cheaters could be less incentivized by having to go through quite the grind before reaching regular lobbies.

The team behind Rob Run is prioritizing strengthening their defenses against cheaters, so much so that an upcoming update that’s expected to deploy new in-game mechanics has been temporarily delayed.

Of course, there’s a lot more work to be done in order to make Rob Run a zone free of cheaters. This isn’t Kefir’s first rodeo with hackers either, as their mobile game, Last Day on Earth: Survival, has also had its fair share of cheaters.

Hopefully, Kefir’s efforts pay off, but cheating remains one of the biggest problems in multiplayer gaming, especially in free-to-play titles. Counter-Strike 2 and Call of Duty: Warzone are just two such games that have been grappling with cheaters over the years. Cheat providers continue to evolve, despite developers rolling out new anti-cheat updates.

On November 17, Rob Run peaked at 549,661 concurrent players on Steam according to SteamDB. After such a strong start, it would be a real shame if the game is unable to reach its full potential due to cheaters holding it back. So far, the developers have kept communication open with players, which does bode well through these struggles.

GTA 6 leaker Arion Kurtaj was sentenced to seven years in prison on November 23, but walked free on licence after time already spent in custody.

#4009. Nioh 3 is, unsurprisingly, the fastest-selling game in the series with over a million units sold

Nioh 3 has taken the Nioh franchise to new heights, delivering its biggest-ever launch.

Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has announced that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

On Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still shows that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”

If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

#4008. The Blood Of Dawnwalker Just Got A Free 1.2 Update, Adding New Game Plus

The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the year's biggest, most ambitious games, and the developers over at Rebel Wolves have done a good job cleaning up bugs and performance issues in the weeks since launch. Today, that trend continued; the new 1.2 update is out now on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, and it adds New Game Plus.

The new mode is uniquely ideal for a game like Dawnwalker. The narrative is very player-driven, whether it has to do with your literal dialogue options, your ability to manage your vampiric hunger, or the order you complete quests, and all of these elements can cause your experience to vary wildly. It makes sense, then, that players would want to jump back in to try things again and see what might happen if the game is played differently, and New Game Plus allows them to do that while keeping combat fresh.

According to the update notes on the Dawnwalker website, "NG+ unlocks after you complete the game’s Epilogue and lets you experience the story again while keeping your progress – mainly your character level, skills, and inventory." You don't gain access to these skills until you complete the prologue, however, which marks the adventure's proper start.

The new mode will also rebalance the world's level scaling. In the base game, certain areas are much harder than others, but in New Game Plus, all enemies will rise in power to match your level, meaning you can explore the world in whatever order you want. On that note, the level cap has also been raised to 100, and protagonist Coen can collect new, more powerful versions of weapons marked with an "NG+" label.

That's basically everything in this update. Rebel Wolves also added some slight tweaks to combat in the base game and adjusted some geometry in the open world, but the main focus here was New Game Plus. This is in contrast to the 1.1 update, which added a much wider suite of bug fixes and made the game run more smoothly.

On a more Nintendo-related note, the Wii celebrated its 20th anniversary, Nintendo was named the most-nominated publisher at this year's The Game Awards, and a brand-new event got underway in Pokémon Pokopia.

So, is anyone playing something other than GTA this weekend?

I wrapped up Ocarina this week, and after a few days of feeling like an empty shell of a man (that ending still rips), I've been back to my backlog in an attempt to clear some before the year is up.

It's been Well Dweller that has been gobbling up most of my time. I think I'm about halfway through now, and it really is delightful. Hopefully I'll make a bit more progress with that this weekend, and maybe finally dip my toe into Pragmata too. Who has time for GTA, eh?

I’ve been absolutely barrelling through Ocarina with the kids, ticking off the Forest, Water, Spirit, and Fire Temples (in that order - a first for me!) in quick succession. A playthrough of the original over the summer definitely helped, so we’re one temple away from the big G, with about 70 Skulltulas bagged and five heart slots left to fill.

Beyond that, Queen’s Domain has me in its grasp, and I’ve also dipped into Well Dweller. Leonida is waiting to be explored on another console, too. Video games, huh? They’re per-ritty good. Have a good one, folks.

To many people’s surprise, I joined the GTA VI bandwagon late last night and was only able to play for an hour. So I’ll likely be following Vice City traffic laws like the previous games and be an upstanding citizen.

I’m also planning on getting some more OOT time in with my main save, getting collectables so I can finally start my “Mai-ster Mode” run. I have a pretty busy weekend regardless, so I hope I can get some gaming sessions in!

I am up to mission 65 in Earth Defense Force 5, and the game continues to throw new enemies (and weapons) my way! Finally, Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 dropped on the eShop, but I must not neglect my The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time progress while serving the Emperor (surely no heresy here). I will also spend this Saturday at Lisboa Games Week, our annual video game celebration expo, and catch up with old friends while making new ones, playing fancy new and upcoming games.

My game of the week is Star Wars Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader. With the GameCube’s recent 25th American release anniversary, this incredible 2001 slice of Star Wars spaceship combat action turned a quarter of a century. I am still waiting for something that surpasses it. Time to chase those secret hidden upgrades and try to go for those gold medals again. Should be “fun” in my old age and diminishing reflexes. I will have to trust the Force on this one...

My wife surprised me with GTA VI, so of course that is what I’m playing, much like the rest of the world. Similar to RDR2, I’m slowly getting a grasp on the controls and life sim mechanics. It can be a grueling process, but it will eventually become second nature.

That being said, I’ve been absolutely blown away by this game. I had been curious for years as to how Rockstar would create an open world experience better than RDR2, and I can safely say that it has been an astonishing and mind-bending.

This is a game that will have people discussing their adventures for years to come. Speaking of, I will share one of my (early) experiences.

I was driving to some rundown RV park nestled away in the middle of nowhere. As I was making my approach I saw a bloodied deer sprawled out on the rocky terrain. Once I got much closer, I see a literal Sasquatch mutilating its body. I was stunned, but I quickly hopped out of my vehicle, got my rifle, and chased after him, but to no avail.

As I make my way back to my vehicle through this thicket of bushes, muddy waters, and even some alligators, I hear gunshots in the distance. I, of course, had to investigate, and find myself stumbling upon a beat down hotel. I notice there is a door wide open, and unexpectedly hear screams. All of a sudden, there is a guy crawling on his hands and knees out of the doorway, bleeding profusely. Another scream happens.

Right there, in the hotel room, was another guy getting mauled and eaten to death by a tiger. I begin panicking as it notices me, and I begin shooting the animal multiple times before it croaks over.

Once the situation becomes calm, I ransack the hotel room. There was a flare gun, drugs, and lots of cash. Out of nowhere comes three hillbillies attempting to rob me. I quickly pull out my flare gun (on accident) and unload my ammo on these punks. They catch fire and succumb to their horrific injuries. The coast is now clear and I book it out of there.

This whole (chance) encounter was so unexpected and organic. It’s these in-between moments that solidifies Rockstar as the masters of their craft. The amount of detail and interactivity is truly awe-inspiring. I can’t wait to see what other events transpire in my next 100-hours of play.

As you probably can already tell, I'm a BIG fan of the Metroid Prime franchise, I consider it one of the best series I've ever played & one of the many very defining Nintendo giants the brand has ever brought to my gaming life.

So, inevitably, I decided to finally jump into the most recent entry of the series with Beyond and I'm absolutely loving it so far, with it being an evolution in several aspects while also not completely neglecting the core gameplay mechanics previous entries introduced to the formula. I love the little details like the visor reflecting Samus' eyes when opening the system menu, the interactivity with the world being close to what Corruption introduced with its motion controls, the emotional but impactful soundtrack & also the great visuals, especially on our 7.9 inch LCD display (I ask myself how great the game will be looking like when Nintendo will release the Switch 2 OLED model!).

Of course I can see where the frustration is coming from when players first experienced Beyond comparing it to the original series, but I also appreciate Nintendo & Retro Studios for taking a different, more cinematic & modern approach to it and I do still have the highest hopes that they will one day release the still remaining two titles of the trilogy remastered on our current day machine.

So, this is what my weekend will be looking like and as I've already said, I'm absolutely loving it. Thank you Alex for your in-depth & benevolent review on YouTube, it is greatly appreciated!

#4006. Xbox One Players Share Their First Impressions Of GTA 6 Via The Cloud

Here's what it's like using Xbox Cloud Gaming to play on XB1

If you want to play GTA 6 natively on any console right now, you can only do so on Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S or PS5. However, if you're willing to use the cloud, it's possible to play the game on Xbox One.

To do this, you have to buy the game on the Xbox Store first, and then acquire Xbox Cloud Gaming time via one of two means - you either purchase time on the Xbox Store, or you get a subscription to Xbox Game Pass that includes a certain amount of time per-tier (and you can top it up later if you need to).

There is also the option to play "free with ads" using Xbox Cloud Gaming, but we haven't verified that it works with GTA 6 yet (although there's seemingly no reason why it wouldn't), and it only gives you 30 minutes of game time before it kicks you off. Some of GTA 6's missions can last longer than 30 minutes, so that's not really ideal.

Anyway, while we're still in the process of dusting off our Xbox One consoles and trying GTA 6 on there for ourselves, we thought we'd first share some impressions from Xbox fans across the web on what it's been like for them so far.

Let's take a look at what some Xbox One owners are saying about it:

Overall, it seems like most people are enjoying their time with GTA 6 on Xbox One so far, although that's not to say there haven't been issues in some cases. The biggest complaints seem to be that some players think it looks "blurry" (while others don't really see a problem), and there are also a small number of reports that it appears to disconnect for no reason sometimes.

There's also a bit of worry that the servers might not be able to handle the load during "peak" hours, and considering we're only on the first day of GTA 6's official launch, it's hard to say how things are going to go in that regard.

Meanwhile, every other version of Xbox Cloud Gaming officially runs at up to 1080p and 12mbps bitrate.

If you want any further feedback about playing GTA 6 on the Xbox One, we'll aim to get some "hands on" impressions to you ASAP. Based on these initial day one impressions though, it seems to be working fairly well right now.

Keep in mind that you obviously need a strong and consistent internet connection in order to play games via Xbox Cloud Gaming, otherwise you may experience heavy lag, disconnects and all sorts of other problems.

Are you playing GTA 6 on Xbox One? Please let us know your impressions of it in the comments below!

#4005. The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an update on what to expect in 2026

Maxis has offered some fresh details on its long-running mission to improve player quality of life in The Sims 4.

As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s new blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

The first stage of the new roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more issues join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

#4003. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4002. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4001. Civilization Developer Firaxis Lays Off A Third Of Its Staff

Firaxis, the studio behind the Civilization series, has laid off around 60 employees, representing a third of its staff. The report comes from Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier.

In a statement provided to Bloomberg by a spokesperson from 2K, a subsidiary of Firaxis' owner, Take-Two, “Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength—designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years. As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

In addition to the 60 affected staffers, Firaxis studio head Heather Hazen is also departing. Bloomberg also reports, via anonymous Firaxis employees speaking to the outlet, that the studio is working on an unannounced XCOM game that has had a challenging development, with the team recently missing an important development milestone. This project, if it releases, will be the first Firaxis-developed XCOM game since XCOM: Chimera Squad in 2020.

Firaxis’ most recent release is Civilization VII, which launched in February 2025 to favorable reviews but initially "slow" sales, according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick last August.  The game currently has a Mixed reception on Steam after Firaxis spent the last year updating the game to address player complaints. Before Civilization VII, Firaxis shipped Marvel's Midnight Suns in 2022, another critically well-received game that failed to meet sales expectations.

#4000. GTA 6's PS5 Platinum Already Unlocked By One Player

There are, quite literally, millions of people playing GTA 6, as Rockstar revealed its hit new game sold more than 32 million copies on its first day. That means the solitary player to have unlocked the game’s Platinum Trophy on PS5 is, quite literally, one in more than 32 million at this moment in time.

PSNProfiles is a website that tracks the trophy stats for every PlayStation game, both for personal use if you want to check in on your own milestones, and as a collective so you can see how you measure up against everyone else.

That means it’s the best place to go to see exactly how many people have unlocked a game’s Platinum rather than going by the rough percentage you’re shown on a game’s actual trophy list. It’s particularly helpful in GTA 6’s case, as that percentage is still locked at zero, but there’s actually one player who has managed to unlock it.

The 28-year-old, critically-acclaimed fighting game has a lot of new, very upset players all of a sudden.

According to PSNProfiles, that world first has been achieved by a player who goes by Danpool85. It also shows that they’ve been playing the game for over a week, which means they had a head start on most of those 32 million who have only been playing for four days. Either they bent the rules or, the more likely scenario, they were provided a review copy early by Rockstar.

They really are the only one right now, too. The Xbox equivalent of PSNProfiles, TrueAchievements, is still showing a zero when it comes to how many players have unlocked GTA 6’s Mythic Achievement. Mythic is the new Platinum-equivalent Xbox achievement added very recently, turning all of those 1,000 Gamerscores into Mythics, dating all the way back to the 360, and seemingly even a few original Xbox titles.

There are 55 trophies to unlock in GTA 6, and its Platinum isn’t currently the only one with so few unlocks that they’re still claiming no one has unlocked them. Performing 250 stunts is another trophy that barely anyone has, as is the trophy you get for scanning 100 different objects using your WAiNK app.

Even though there’s still so much more left to do and see, as demonstrated by literally one person in the world reaching 100% completion so far, some of the secrets the millions of us playing have collectively discovered so far are nothing short of incredible.

In less than a week, players have already managed to stop the GTA 6 train - something that was infamously impossible in previous entries - and discovered an easter egg that mentions the GTA 5 protagonists by name, confirming the games take place in the same shared universe. The tip of the hat to the last GTA can be found in a GTA 6 true crime podcast where the host interviews Wade, another character from GTA 5. Wade comments on Trevor, Franklin, and Michael not being responsible for the murders of Deborah and Floyd, blissfully unaware that they did kill those characters and then framed him for their murders.

GTA 6 was a monumental launch for Rockstar, with over 50% of all active console users playing the game on day one.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

Now, is 400k a good result on its own for a game that cost at least $300 million to make (with some estimates putting it a lot more than that)? I'd argue no, that would be pretty dismal. However, with that said, we were also led to believe that it had sold 711,000 Premium Upgrades ahead of its launch, which is not to be sniffed at, and obviously we do not know how many more consoles were sold, nor how many more Game Pass subscriptions were sold. Nor do we know how much money people have been spending on the microtransactions either. All of that does add up.

The problem though comes down to simple maths, if E-Day cost $200 million (and bear in mind that is a conservative figure because we are led to believe it cost much more than that to make), but still, if it cost $200 million to make, then the game needs to sell the equivalent of 2,850,000 full priced games in order to just break even, and it is a long way short of that in sheer sales. And of course, if the game cost the reported $300 million then it needs to sell the equivalent of 4,285,000 full priced copies. This is where the problem for the game lies as it is highly unlikely to make back its development costs, which could be very bad news for the studio.

Obviously, we know that a single exclusive is not what it is all about for Xbox; it is about creating an ecosystem that will attract people in considerable numbers, and also ensure that people already here do not want to leave. However, the problem is, there are no exclusive games are on the near horizon that will continue to attract people. It's possible that the Elder Scrolls 6 will be exclusive to Xbox, and a lot of people within these forums are pinning their hopes for Xbox on that game, but the problem there is that ES6 could be several years away.

My honest opinion is that I think that Sharma will look at E-Day's (probably) meagre sales and behind the scenes the decision to reverse course on exclusives will be made, although I do not expect her to tell us this is the case until after Helix releases as I don't think Sharma will want to hurt the sales chances of Helix by publicly admitting that it won't have exclusive games. I say this on the basis that there are no big AAA console selling games on the horizon, and that Helix is likely to release prior to the next big first-party game. I mean, there's not a lot of point in telling us right now that Xbox will no longer have exclusive first-party games when there are none in the near future anyway. She may as well wait until she can no longer avoid telling us that's the case because the game is being put up for pre-orders.

Time will tell, and I'd love to be proven wrong, but I would far rather see studios survive and our favourite games continue to be made, than pursue a self-harming exclusive strategy. Of course, all that could change if (when!) Sharma announces a change in day one first-party Game Pass releases, but I think that should have been done prior to the release of E-Day, and the next big AAA first-party game is probably years away...
